story.title: Tether: iMessage, SMS, etc. on Linux

draft:
Tether promises iMessage, SMS and other Apple‑centric messaging on Linux—finally a bridge between two worlds that have lived apart for too long.  

I’ve been testing the prototype on my Ubuntu workstation. The UI feels native enough to stay out of the way, yet the reliance on a macOS relay server raises questions about latency and privacy. If the relay is open‑source, the community could audit it; otherwise we might be trading convenience for a new attack surface.

What I find most intriguing is how this could shift the narrative around Linux as a “secondary” device. When you can answer a client’s iMessage without switching to a Mac, the platform becomes a first‑class productivity hub rather than a niche dev box.

Do you think the trade‑offs in security and dependency are worth the convenience of unified messaging on Linux?
